notes: The native implementation is a deterministic prototype with CIGAR-aware anchored indels, short-distance compound I/D candidates, optional graph-phased MNP grouping via --max-mnp-distance (default 0, matching GATK's independent-SNP default), reference-backed bucketed PairHMM, Kokkos graph/path telemetry, Kokkos GATK-shaped per-read normalization and REF/ALT max-marginalization, strict reference-connected graph-SNP posterior ownership, likelihood-based graph-haplotype pruning and reference-block plus candidate-site gVCF output; candidate sets above --max-haplotype-combination-alleles are split into stable coordinate blocks with complete per-block 2^N combinations, a bounded candidate-to-haplotype link budget, shared REF haplotype and stable read×haplotype request deduplication; bounded graph k-mer/path controls are explicit and recorded in telemetry. --kmer-size is repeatable and normalized to GATK's sorted request list (default [10,25]); the legacy scalar remains the final explicit value for older consumers.

--native-pair-hmm-use-double-precision is an optional boolean: omission preserves the strict double path, explicit true selects simd<double>, and explicit false selects the bucketed Kokkos simd<float> throughput path. The effective precision is recorded in summary/OutputManifest; Float32 is tolerance-only and flow-tagged inputs explicitly use regular base-space Float32 rather than claiming a float flow recurrence.

VCF and candidate-site gVCF share PairHMM per-read likelihoods for full concrete multi-ALT diploid PLs; reference-only blocks carry REF-vs-any AD/PL/GQ and GQ-band MIN_DP state; gVCF <NON_REF> rows use a finite concrete-likelihood envelope. Reference-backed VCF/GVCF also accepts --sample-ploidy 1..8 with VCF Number=G PL/GT/GQ/AC/AN and ploidy-specific REF/<NON_REF> blocks; no-reference polyploid likelihoods fail closed. The RCM path now exposes GATK's configurable indel-size bound and read/reference suffix plausibility test; unseen-haplotype posterior and full posterior-block semantics remain pending.

-ERC BP_RESOLUTION reuses the Kokkos RCM kernel without GQ-band coalescing and emits one REF/<NON_REF> row per base; HTSlib @RG SM is preserved as the VCF/GVCF sample column, and absent sample metadata fails closed instead of inventing a sample.

Ordinary -ERC GVCF rebuilds reference blocks after final genotype selection: uncalled SNP/MNP candidates fold back into <NON_REF> blocks, while uncalled indels reserve their REF span as candidate records. Standard blocks use FILTER=., INFO=END, GT:DP:GQ:MIN_DP:PL; candidate records use GT:AD:DP:GQ:PL:SB. Zero-support assembly-only indels fold back under --min-alt-support. Manifest fields gvcf_standard_fields, gvcf_candidate_standard_fields and gvcf_candidate_rebuild_after_genotyping make this contract explicit; the bundled oracle checks candidate-site equality and non-overlap, but RCM boundaries/values remain non-bit-identical.

The candidate-site GVCF writer now matches the pinned GATK 4.6.2.0 rows for QUAL/FILTER, ordered INFO (including MLEAC/MLEAF/RAW_MQandDP), GT:AD:DP:GQ:PL:SB and uncapped Number=G PL; zero-support assembly-only indels are folded back under --min-alt-support. Manifest gvcf_candidate_standard_fields records this contract; complete block-boundary and provenance parity remains outside the oracle.

The shared Kokkos RCM Number=G materializer preserves GATK's uncapped integer PL range (the PairHMM candidate-envelope 999 cap is not applied to ReferenceConfidenceModel). The pinned fastgatk-hc-rcm-pl-range-gatk-oracle covers BP_RESOLUTION with --indel-size-to-eliminate-in-ref-model 1 and a high-depth PL=1080 row on OpenMP and Serial; full RCM/assembly numeric parity and provenance remain outside this bounded gate.

HC call confidence follows the GATK CLI contract: ordinary VCF defaults to standard-min-confidence-threshold-for-calling=30, GVCF/BP_RESOLUTION forces zero, and a batched Kokkos AF/Dirichlet EM kernel computes candidate QUAL; broader native assembly/PairHMM likelihood parity remains pending.

The normal VCF writer now emits the GATK 4.6.2.0 schema definitions for INFO/FORMAT/FILTER (including InbreedingCoeff and exact rank-sum descriptions), preserves @SQ AS assembly tags, and places the stable source line after the contig dictionary; only release command-line/date provenance remains intentionally dynamic.

--sample-name selects one @RG SM sample at the HTSlib Host boundary, filters reads before the shared Kokkos calling pipeline, reorders the selected sample first for the VCF/GVCF column, and records sample_name_selection in summary/manifest; an absent sample fails closed.

Materialized graph haplotypes now expose reference-connected SW/Host traceback provenance (GATK NEW_SW_PARAMETERS score, CIGAR, alignment score, absolute offset, deterministic signature, and graph_haplotype_sw_* Kokkos execution telemetry) in graph_haplotype_path_details; read x haplotype PairHMM requests additionally report valid/indel CIGAR counts, post-marginalization 0.2-log10 BestAllele uncertainty telemetry, CIGAR/soft-clip evidence-gate counts and flow read key/matrix clipping counts; overlapping bounded AssemblyRegion halos are coalesced before graph/PairHMM and union/rescue counts are explicit; cyclic/non-unique reference retry follows GATK's final expanded-kmer allowance; the real assembly-graph oracle requires one valid CIGAR per path and Kokkos graph scoring, while full posterior, hmer and release-complete cross-AssemblyRegion semantics remain explicit.

AssemblyRegion defaults now match GATK 4.6.2.0 (100-base assembly halo and 50-base activity probability propagation). Host trim filtering uses GATK's original AlignmentUtils.unclippedReadLength (minus soft clips), not the post-trim fragment length; this preserves short edge fragments for PairHMM. The pinned fastgatk-hc-assembly-region-boundary-gatk-oracle exercises --max-assembly-region-size 50 and verifies byte-identical VCF output, including 17:69368 AD=20,22/DP=42, on OpenMP and Serial. This is a bounded active-region/read-ownership contract, not complete HC graph/assembly parity.

Explicit CIGAR insertion/deletion events are now projected into the shared Kokkos ActivityProfile as indel seeds, matching GATK's active AssemblyRegion ownership when aligned bases are reference-matching. The pinned fastgatk-hc-cigar-indel-activity-gatk-oracle uses 8x 60M2D58M plus 8x 120M reads and verifies the normalized chr1:250 GCA>G call, genotype payload, one owned region, and zero PairHMM-unassigned candidates on OpenMP and Serial; full graph/assembly parity remains outside this bounded gate.
It is not yet bit-identical or biologically equivalent to GATK HaplotypeCaller.

When FASTA is available, the Kokkos activity profile consumes the Host reference projection and records activity_reference_projection=true; no-reference smoke inputs retain an explicit diversity fallback.

The shared Kokkos read-filter mask matches GATK's MAPQ>=20, MappingQualityAvailable (MAPQ=255 exclusion), and duplicate exclusion defaults; built-in filter classes include GoodCigar/Wellformed/NonZeroReferenceLengthAlignment CIGAR checks, while custom classes fail closed and use --fallback for explicit Java execution.

-XL/--exclude-intervals is applied after -L/--intervals at projected-locus granularity; -ip/-ixp padding is normalized by the shared HtsReader and carried into assembly, graph, PairHMM and reference-confidence output. Reads crossing an excluded and included locus retain evidence for the included locus.

Repeated -I/--input shards are combined in Host order after sequence-dictionary validation; without --sample-name the input sample sets must also match. Contig streaming uses a bounded coordinate k-way merge, and region streaming merges indexed halo tiles across shards.

-isr/--interval-set-rule now supports GATK UNION (default) and INTERSECTION across repeatable -L/--intervals selectors; the selected rule is applied in the shared HtsReader before padding and recorded in telemetry/manifest.

--create-output-variant-index accepts GATK optional boolean syntax (flag, true/false, or =true/=false); compressed VCF/GVCF receives .tbi and plain VCF receives a Tribble .idx when enabled, while false suppresses both sidecars and the manifest records the choice.

--disable-sequence-dictionary-validation is an explicit optional boolean: by default the Host validates reference FASTA/FAI contig order and lengths against each input BAM; when enabled, the check is skipped and the choice is recorded in summary/manifest.

Explicit -ERC/--emit-ref-confidence NONE overrides a .g.vcf output suffix and keeps ordinary VCF semantics; GVCF and BP_RESOLUTION retain their reference-confidence paths, and unknown ERC modes fail closed.

PCR indel model compatibility is shared by HC and Mutect2: --pcr-indel-model accepts NONE, HOSTILE, AGGRESSIVE, and CONSERVATIVE; tandem-repeat quality adjustment is applied in Host preparation before Kokkos PairHMM and its model/rate/adjusted-position telemetry is recorded.

--sites-only-vcf-output accepts GATK optional Boolean syntax (bare or separated true/false) at the final writer boundary: HaplotypeCaller retains full FORMAT/sample evidence for genotyping and reference-confidence computation, then emits an 8-column site-only VCF/GVCF when enabled. The pinned GATK 4.6.2.0 oracle covers VCF/GVCF true, false and bare forms; manifest telemetry records the choice.

--floor-blocks accepts GATK optional Boolean syntax for ordinary GVCF reference blocks: after RCM/genotyping it floors GQ to the active GQ-band lower bound, serializes compact GT:DP:GQ blocks and omits MIN_DP/PL, while candidate-site records and BP_RESOLUTION are unchanged. The pinned GQ-band oracle compares the Java rows and manifest boundary.

Native prototype reuses the HC/Kokkos kernel path for tumor/normal, emits TLOD/AF from biallelic or all-alleles-vs-without-ALT Dirichlet variational evidence plus a Kokkos somatic-germline-artifact-orientation posterior (PSOMATIC/PGERMLINE/PARTIFACT/OBP/CONTAM), groups concrete sibling ALTs into one multi-ALT locus record with Number=A vectors and REF+ALT AD/FAD, writes common Mutect2-shaped INFO (AS_SB_TABLE/DP/ECNT/ECNTH/MBQ/MFRL/MMQ/MPOS/POPAF) and GATK-shaped GT/AD/AF/DP/F1R2/F2R1/FAD/SB tumor fields, germline filtering, stats and F1R2 sidecars, and writes VCF/Tabix output. Mutect2 has an explicit somatic candidate-emission boundary: pileup candidates without a retained PairHMM ALT owner are restored and accept separate GATK --initial-tumor-lod (default 2, activity seed) and --tumor-lod-to-emit (default 3, final emission); until activity-region parity is complete, native applies their stricter value at output and records both plus the effective threshold, while raw -L selectors constrain halo-derived candidates to the requested core interval; fallback counts and candidate summaries are recorded. --af-of-alleles-not-in-resource (aliases --population-af/-default-af) controls the POPAF fallback, using 5e-8 tumor-only and 1e-6 tumor-normal by default. --mitochondria-mode accepts bare/optional boolean syntax and applies GATK mitochondrial defaults (both LOD thresholds 0, population AF 4e-3, pruning -4*ln(10), recover all dangling branches) unless explicitly overridden; effective values are recorded in stats/manifest. --dont-use-soft-clipped-bases is shared with HaplotypeCaller and gates terminal/internal soft-clip-derived assembly evidence while preserving explicit CIGAR I/D events. An explicit .tar.gz --f1r2-tar-gz path emits the standard .ref_histogram/.alt_histogram/.alt_table archive; explicit .tsv keeps the legacy sidecar.

The Mutect2 default read-filter mask includes OA/XM-backed NonChimericOriginalAlignmentReadFilter, ReadLengthReadFilter(30, Integer.MAX_VALUE), MappingQualityAvailableReadFilter (reject MAPQ=255), and MappingQualityNotZeroReadFilter (reject MAPQ=0). The Host reader preserves optional tags through shard/tile merges and the Kokkos predicate compares OA's first comma-delimited contig with XM; a missing tag passes as in GATK. Effective length bounds and MAPQ sentinel policy are recorded in telemetry.

PCR indel model parity is shared with HaplotypeCaller: --pcr-indel-model accepts NONE, HOSTILE, AGGRESSIVE, and CONSERVATIVE and applies GATK-shaped tandem-repeat quality adjustment before Kokkos PairHMM; selected model, rate factor and adjusted positions are recorded in stats/manifest telemetry.

Accepts GATK --tumor-sample/--normal-sample aliases; selected tumor and normal samples are filtered at the HTSlib @RG ID->SM Host boundary before assembly/PairHMM, and the selected names plus filtered read counts are recorded in stats/manifest. A single multi-sample -I can supply both tumor and normal via --tumor-sample/--normal-sample (or -normal); --normal-input remains supported for separate files. Repeatable -normal/--normal-sample selectors are deduplicated in argv order, aggregate their evidence for somatic inference, and emit one independent normal genotype column per selected sample. Aggregate mode accepts repeatable -I shards with sequence-dictionary/@SQ AS validation and deterministic sample-filtered coordinate merging (argv order is the tie-break); indexed --stream-by-region probes every shard, validates all indexes/dictionaries, and performs the same stable coordinate merge per core/halo tile. Absent tumor selection resolves to the first tumor-header sample; a tumor header with no @RG SM fails closed before decoding, matching GATK's samples-cannot-be-empty contract, rather than silently labeling all reads TUMOR. verify_mutect2_gatk_oracle.py checks the sample/index/sidecar contract and reports, rather than suppresses, site-set/posterior divergence.
Release-specific GATK prior calibration, read-orientation model fitting and full joint FilterMutectCalls semantics remain explicit fallback; use --fallback for production-equivalent Mutect2.

--minimum-allele-fraction/-min-AF is forwarded to the Kokkos SomaticLikelihoodsEngine ALT pseudocount prior (default 0 keeps the flat [1,1] prior), and the selected value is recorded in stats/manifest.

Repeated -L/--intervals now supports GATK -isr/--interval-set-rule UNION (default) or INTERSECTION; the same normalized selector set is used by aggregate and indexed --stream-by-region paths and recorded in stats/manifest.

--sites-only-vcf-output true|false is supported at the final VCF writer boundary: caller, posterior and F1R2 computation are unchanged, while FORMAT/sample columns are omitted and the choice is recorded in stats/manifest.

--create-output-variant-index is an optional GATK boolean (default true): compressed VCF output receives a sibling .tbi and uncompressed VCF output receives a Tribble .idx only when enabled; disabling it is recorded in stats/manifest and never changes caller/posterior/sidecar evidence.

--phred-scaled-global-read-mismapping-rate follows GATK's release-pinned boundary: positive Q enables the per-read cap, negative Q passes the -Infinity disabled-cap sentinel through shared Kokkos normalization (preserving valid -Infinity cells), and zero is rejected (it is not an uncapped mode); the choice is applied before Kokkos somatic TLOD evidence and reported by the bounded Mutect2 mismatch-rate oracle.

Mutect2's pinned fastgatk-pairhmm-results-gatk-oracle now requires GATK 4.6.2.0 and native to materialize the same 706 serialized PairHMM requests over 18 local haplotypes. The request boundary accounts for post-trim read-stub removal and same-fragment phased branches before the shared Kokkos recurrence; fastgatk-mutect2-gatk-oracle fails on any count divergence.

PairHMM missing BI/BD input follows GATK ReadUtils: raw default insertion/deletion quality is Q45, Conservative PCR adjustment lowers only non-terminal positions (effective Q40 at repeat length zero), and the terminal position remains Q45. Explicit BI/BD tags retain their existing Host decode/PCR path; the pinned pairhmm-default-indel-quality oracle checks Java serialized inputs plus native telemetry.

--force-active is an optional GATK boolean. It preserves the pinned ActivityProfile boundaries while forcing every profile segment through AssemblyRegion graph/PairHMM processing; the value is recorded in stats/manifest and fastgatk-mutect2-force-active-gatk-oracle checks Java/native IGV state and candidate-site stability.

--normal-lod (default 2.2) applies GATK's fixed diploid hom-ref minus ref/ALT-het log10 likelihood ratio after native fragment likelihoods are materialized; this NLOD is kept separate from variational TLOD evidence. fastgatk-somatic-normal-lod-gatk-oracle pins the equation and fastgatk-mutect2-normal-lod-gatk-oracle pins the GATK 4.6.2.0 emission boundary on OpenMP and Serial.

It emits standard GATK .ref_histogram/.alt_histogram/.alt_table members in a real .tar.gz; the chr17 fixture matches GATK 4.6.2.0 histogram and alt-table counts, including -XL/--exclude-intervals site subtraction when -L is present. Native prototype applies deterministic TLOD/germline FILTER annotations plus optional AF contamination-floor, minimum AF, strand support, unique ALT read, median base/mapping/read-position, MFRL fragment-length, NCount ratio, PSOMATIC/PGERMLINE/PARTIFACT posterior, clustered-event (ECNT/ECNTH) and multiallelic filters, with stats sidecar and BGZF/Tabix or plain VCF/Tribble .idx output.

Common hard-filter defaults match GATK M2FiltersArgumentCollection: MBQ=20, MMQ=30, MPOS=1, maximum ref/ALT MFRL difference=10000 and max NCount/ALT ratio=+Infinity; explicit negative values retain a documented disable path, and zero ALT depth skips NRatioFilter like Java. --mitochondria-mode/--microbial-mode accept bare or optional boolean values (next-token or =true/false), disable genomic-only clustered/multiallelic/fragment/haplotype filters; microbial keeps slippage with MMQ=20, mitochondrial suppresses slippage and uses log-SNV/log-indel defaults -2.5*ln(10)/-3.75*ln(10) unless overridden, and the mode/effective priors are recorded in telemetry.

-L/--intervals/--interval/--region selectors support GATK-style literal, interval-file, and VCF selectors with --interval-set-rule UNION (default) or INTERSECTION; the selected subset is applied consistently to orientation, haplotype, empirical-learning, and final filtering passes and is recorded in manifest/telemetry.

Allele-specific GATK fields are honored at the VCF boundary: AS_SB_TABLE supplies ALT strand counts when scalar F1R2/R1F2 are absent, and AS_UNIQ_ALT_READ_COUNT takes precedence over total AD for unique-alt filtering.

Rust/GATK hard-filter boundary emits AS_FilterStatus (Number=A,Type=String), applies per-ALT MBQ/MMQ/MPOS, strict zero-strand, <= unique-read, natural-log TLOD multiallelic, presence-based PON, and all-sample ALT-AD NRatio semantics. Number=A TLOD/posterior vectors are reduced by concrete ALT (max TLOD, min somatic posterior, max germline/artifact posterior), while contamination/minimum-AF use all tumor ALT fractions; scalar legacy annotations broadcast and missing vector elements retain position. Full ErrorProbabilities joint posterior remains explicit fallback.

When NALOD and ##normal_sample are present, a Kokkos NormalArtifactFilter subset applies the 10% normal-AF ratio gate, normal-pileup binomial tail, and NALOD posterior; the posterior is compared with the effective FilterMutectCalls error threshold (not merely >0) before emitting normal_artifact, with telemetry. Empirical multi-pass thresholds and cross-filter ErrorProbabilities remain explicit fallback.

An existing --stats path that matches a GATK Mutect2 stats table is treated as read-only input and the native filtering-stats JSON is written beside the output (or to --filtering-stats); this prevents the compatibility layer from overwriting the upstream stats artifact. Such calls default to GATK OPTIMAL_F_SCORE empirical learning when --threshold-strategy is omitted. JSON includes FilteringOutputStats-style per-filter FP/FDR/FN/FNR; a .table/.tsv filtering-stats path emits the GATK table plus a .json sidecar. Per-ALT probabilities are keyed by original VCF ALT index so an interleaved symbolic <NON_REF> cannot shift concrete-ALT attribution; PARTIFACT and OBP are reduced as correlated ARTIFACT filters with per-ALT max, then combined independently with NON_SOMATIC and SEQUENCING using 1-prod(1-p), matching Java ErrorProbabilities. The input threshold/model is recorded but release-specific empirical application remains explicit fallback.

TumorEvidenceFilter weak_evidence now evaluates the unlearned flat/high-AF SomaticClusteringModel with a Kokkos log-beta kernel per ALT; PolymeraseSlippageFilter evaluates the RPA/RU one-slip gate with a Kokkos regularized-beta kernel and emits STRQ/slippage. The native threshold is explicit --filter-error-probability-threshold (default 0.1); four-pass empirical model/threshold learning remains fallback.

With explicit --threshold-strategy, a streaming ErrorProbabilities subset combines PSOMATIC/PGERMLINE/PARTIFACT/OBP (TLOD+AD fallback), reducing PARTIFACT/OBP within ARTIFACT by max and combining ARTIFACT/NON_SOMATIC/SEQUENCING with the GATK independent-error product; it learns CONSTANT/FDR/F-score threshold and emits per-ALT error_probability; filter-specific Java maps and the complete empirical SomaticClusteringModel remain fallback.

Plain and gzip-compressed pileup tables are accepted, and .gz output/segmentation suffixes use zlib streaming; manifest records compressed_io/input_compressed/output_compressed. The native changepoint stage follows Java KernelSegmenter seeded sampling, kernel approximation, persistence and backward-selection parameters; segmentation contig output reproduces Java groupingBy/HashMap bucket order and numeric fields use binary64 shortest-round-trip formatting. Java DoubleStream compensated sums make contamination/error raw-bit exact on the pinned CPU fixtures; Commons Math 3.5 elementwise SVD parity, MAF/report ULP identity, cloud inputs and final bit-identical semantics remain explicit fallback.

The OutputManifest records compressed-IO counts and Kokkos likelihood/segmenter kernel telemetry, and the file-boundary benchmark (benchmark_calculate_contamination.py, warmup/p50/p95 with plan-reuse assertions) is wired into verify_all.sh.

Native prototype reads BAM/CRAM/SAM through the shared HTSlib Host reader, applies the GATK default mapping/duplicate/primary/vendor/mate/CIGAR/Wellformed mask, and uses a Kokkos count kernel for ref/ALT/other base categories at AF-qualified biallelic SNP sites.

ReadLengthReadFilter is available through typed --min-read-length/--max-read-length bounds and is recorded in the manifest; the same bounds are evaluated before pileup projection so filtered reads cannot contribute bases.

Supported built-in --read-filter, --inverted-read-filter/-XRF and --disable-read-filter names are validated and applied explicitly; --disable-tool-default-read-filters now starts from an empty filter set rather than silently ignoring custom filters. Inverted filters apply the GATK InvertedReadFilter predicate after the ordinary default/-RF mask.

Coordinate and VCF-site -L selectors use HTSlib indexed iteration for indexed population VCF/BCF resources (including tabix TBI sequence-name mapping) and record indexed traversal/query telemetry; unindexed resources retain sequential fallback.

GATK-compatible -XL/--exclude-intervals is applied after -L, including VCF-site selectors; -ip and -ixp expand include/exclude intervals with saturating zero-based half-open arithmetic, and separate-token boolean forms are accepted for disable-tool-default-read-filters and dictionary validation.
Ref/ALT, observation, and count Kokkos Views are retained across read batches and grow only when capacity is exceeded; persistent allocation/reuse telemetry is written to OutputManifest.

GoodCigarReadFilter is evaluated per decoded record through ReadBatch::cigar_record_layout_valid(); reference_end/project_read_offset use the same record-local CIGAR contract, so malformed CIGAR metadata cannot discard valid sibling reads in one batch. OpenMP/Serial mixed-batch regression is covered.

When AF-bearing records exist but none pass AF/interval or biallelic-SNP selection, native emits a successful metadata/header-only table like GATK; missing AF header/values remains a fail-closed BAD_INPUT.

The table columns and SAMPLE metadata are GATK-shaped; the first @RG SM sample is used and a missing sample fails closed (no SAMPLE=UNKNOWN). Text VCF AF tokens retain GATK/htsjdk binary64 parsing and shortest round-trip formatting (typed BCF retains HTSlib's float decode), and the bundled GATK 4.6.2.0 table oracle is byte-exact on long-decimal/scientific AF plus read-filter fixtures. Repeated -L/--intervals support GATK UNION (default) or INTERSECTION via -isr/--interval-set-rule, recorded in summary/manifest. Full LocusWalker pileup filtering, cloud inputs, dictionary edge cases and broader Java report semantics remain explicit fallback.
The OutputManifest records traversal/query telemetry, and the file-boundary benchmark (benchmark_get_pileup_summaries.py, warmup/p50/p95) is wired into verify_all.sh.

Native Host/HTSlib/FAIDX prototype validates VCF parsing, REF/reference agreement, ALT uniqueness/non-empty/REF-equality and GATK VariantContext.validateAlternateAlleles() usage (each concrete ALT must occur in a called genotype), AN/GT chromosome counts, optional dbSNP IDs, interval subsets and GVCF <NON_REF>/order/overlap checks; --validate-gvcf unions every record span (including concrete variants) and checks complete per-contig or requested-interval coverage, leading/trailing contig coverage and END bounds; GVCF mode explicitly disables strict ALLELES validation like GATK; warnings, sequence-dictionary length checks and OutputManifest issue records are deterministic.

-XL/--exclude-intervals is applied after -L/--intervals, with -ip/-ixp padding in the shared zero-based half-open interval space; repeated -L/--intervals support GATK UNION (default) or INTERSECTION via -isr/--interval-set-rule, and the selected rule is recorded in telemetry/manifest. GATK single-dash Barclay synonyms -D, -isr, -do-not-validate-filtered-records, -warn-on-errors and -disable-sequence-dictionary-validation are accepted alongside their long names and covered by the pinned command oracle. Excluded spans are removed from GVCF coverage targets. GATK/Barclay Boolean options accept explicit true/false/1/0 as well as the native bare-switch form; native rejects invalid literals and rejects --do-not-validate-filtered-records combined with --validate-GVCF or --fail-gvcf-on-overlap before opening input. --disable-sequence-dictionary-validation is honored explicitly. Full htsjdk/Tribble validation, complete dbSNP overlap semantics, release-specific GVCF annotation/posterior semantics and GATK exception/report wording are not bit-identical; unsupported validation behavior remains explicit fallback.

Symbolic ALT alleles such as <DEL> and <CNV> are excluded from the validateAlternateAlleles called-genotype usage check, while concrete ALT alleles remain strict; the pinned GATK 4.6.2.0 symbolic-ALT oracle covers unobserved symbolic, mixed symbolic/concrete, and concrete-failure cases.

The OutputManifest records runtime resource telemetry via the shared ResourceSnapshot JSON, and the file-boundary benchmark (benchmark_validate_variants.py, warmup/p50/p95) is wired into verify_all.sh.

Native streams coordinate-sorted VCF/BCF shards, merges later header definitions, validates sample order and contig dictionary name/order/length, rejects interval-overlapping records (including gVCF END spans) by default, and writes BGZF/Tabix or plain VCF/Tribble .idx output with a completion manifest. Picard/GATK uppercase --INPUT/--OUTPUT/--REFERENCE_SEQUENCE long aliases are accepted alongside -I/-O/-R, and --QUIET/--VERBOSITY are parsed with their Boolean/log-level values.

Default mode requires coordinate-sorted disjoint intervals; repeated -L/--intervals regions are applied before this check and support GATK UNION (default) or INTERSECTION via -isr/--interval-set-rule, with the selected rule recorded in summary/manifest. --allow-overlaps is explicit without deduplication. --reorder-input-by-first-variant/-RI true performs a stable first-record sort with the first shard's sequence dictionary, matching GATK REORDER_INPUT_BY_FIRST_VARIANT. -CO/--COMMENT emits GatherVcfs.comment metadata, --CREATE_INDEX controls tabix creation, and --COMPRESSION_LEVEL matches Picard's BGZF level contract. --disable-sequence-dictionary-validation is an explicit escape hatch recorded in OutputManifest. Native BCF output is fail-closed because HTSlib emits BCF 2.2 while pinned GATK/htsjdk requires its BCF 2.1 form; use explicit --fallback for .bcf output. Dispatcher HTTP(S)/presigned staging covers remote I/O; direct-binary remote reads and full GATK gather metadata remain explicit fallback. The contract-compatible scope is local or dispatcher-staged VCF shards in supported VCF output modes.

Native prototype performs reference-backed common prefix/suffix trimming and deterministic repeat left-shifting for primitive non-symbolic alleles, with optional multiallelic splitting, shared Kokkos arbitrary-ploidy PL/AD remap, GATK REF projection for removed ALTs, PL minimum normalization, GT/GQ compaction, split AC/AN/AF recomputation and AC_Orig/AF_Orig/AN_Orig preservation, repeated -L/--intervals filtering with GATK UNION (default) or INTERSECTION set rules, -XL exclusion with -ip/-ixp padding, and BGZF/Tabix or plain VCF/Tribble .idx output. Include/exclude selectors use END-span overlap and all selected boundaries are recorded in the manifest. Boolean controls accept Barclay bare/separated forms, and -isr/-imr/-OVI aliases are accepted. The optional --sites-only-vcf-output Boolean is applied at the final writer boundary after normalization, emitting GATK-shaped 8-column site records while retaining full FORMAT/sample evidence during processing; its shape and true/false/bare forms are pinned against GATK 4.6.2.0.

Multiallelic records containing symbolic ALT alleles use the GATK fail-closed split contract (no-call GT, clear non-GT FORMAT and INFO, telemetry counts); --max-indel-length and --max-leading-bases match GATK's inclusive size and bounded repeat walk. Complex symbolic reference normalization, interval-list/cloud semantics and bit-identical normalization remain explicit fallback.
The OutputManifest records split/trim/skip telemetry, and the file-boundary benchmark (benchmark_left_align.py, warmup/p50/p95) is wired into verify_all.sh.

Native prototype evaluates a deterministic JEXL subset (QUAL/INFO/FORMAT, vc.getAttribute, common VariantContext site methods, genotype predicates and indexed getAD/getPL FORMAT methods, including GATK compact per-sample forms such as GQ < 20, AD[1] == 0 and isHet == 1, explicit boolean RHS comparisons, boolean operators, string methods, =~/!~ regex operators and null checks), supports GATK INFO-vector access vc.getAttribute("TAG").get(i) plus TAG[i] shorthand, site/genotype filter inversion, VCF/BCF mask intervals with extension and GATK --filter-not-in-mask reverse logic, deterministic clustered-event windows, preserves existing genotype FT labels and appends lexical-ordered/deduplicated FILTER/FT labels, and writes BGZF/Tabix or plain VCF/Tribble .idx output plus manifest. Repeated -L/--intervals accept GATK UNION (default) or INTERSECTION set rules before record filtering. --missing-values-evaluate-as-failing follows GATK's Boolean boundary (bare or separated true/false; embedded '=' rejected), with missing numeric values and explicit == null kept on separate paths.

Common site methods include isSNP/isIndel/isMNP/isTransition/isTransversion/isMixed/isSymbolic/isVariant/isBiallelic/isMultiallelic/isFiltered/isPass/isNotFiltered/isNoVariation, hasAttribute/hasAlternateAllele, getStart/getEnd/getNAlleles/getNSamples, getType and contig/ID/reference/alternate string accessors with contains/startsWith/endsWith/regex and enum/null comparisons. Reference/ALT Allele methods isSymbolic/isReference/isNoCall/isNonReference/length are supported with HTSJDK symbolic length semantics. --apply-allele-specific-filters evaluates common numeric AS_* Number=A annotations per ALT and writes AS_FilterStatus; --invalidate-previous-filters follows GATK by clearing only existing site FILTER labels while retaining genotype FT history; --mask-description emits a custom mask FILTER header description and GATK default/reverse mask descriptions are selected; repeated -L/--intervals regions are applied before filtering, while complete JEXL method and complex allele-specific annotation semantics remain explicit fallback, and unsupported expressions are rejected rather than ignored.

--set-filtered-genotype-to-no-call accepts GATK bare or separated Boolean syntax (embedded '=' is rejected), converts called genotypes with non-PASS FORMAT/FT to unphased ./., and recomputes INFO/AC, INFO/AN and INFO/AF only when a genotype changed; existing genotype FT labels are retained.

The OutputManifest records runtime resource telemetry via the shared ResourceSnapshot JSON, and the file-boundary benchmark (benchmark_variant_filtration.py, warmup/p50/p95) is wired into verify_all.sh.

Native prototype implements coordinate/queryname external-memory sorting with bounded in-memory records, HTSJDK-compatible strand/flag/MAPQ/mate/TLEN/HI tie-breaks, spill runs, deterministic k-way merge, scratch telemetry and BAM/CRAM index output. Explicit --resume-spill checkpoints a complete input pass and validates input size/mtime plus spill-run completeness before an output-stage retry; --add-pg-tag emits a configurable @PG record.
GATK optional booleans for --add-pg-tag and output-index switches accept bare/true/1 or false/0 and reject other literals before touching input/output files.

Picard/GATK 4.6.2.0 long aliases --INPUT/--OUTPUT/--REFERENCE_SEQUENCE, -SO/--SORT_ORDER, --MAX_RECORDS_IN_RAM/--TMP_DIR, --CREATE_INDEX, --QUIET, --USE_JDK_DEFLATER/INFLATER, --COMPRESSION_LEVEL, --VALIDATION_STRINGENCY, and --VERBOSITY are parsed with the same bounded sort/writer contract; compression and validation choices are recorded in OutputManifest telemetry while HTSlib remains the codec backend.

Full Picard duplicate/read-group/cloud staging and all SortSam release-specific options remain explicit fallback; spill failures are RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED rather than silent in-memory growth. The OutputManifest records runtime resource telemetry (RSS, scratch and spill-run bytes) via the shared ResourceSnapshot JSON, and the file-boundary benchmark (benchmark_sort_sam.py, warmup/p50/p95 with a forced spill run) is wired into verify_all.sh and both CTest backends.

Native prototype performs a deterministic two-pass coordinate-sorted canonical paired-fragment duplicate-key grouping, so distant mates share one fragment representative; it also provides read-group/library partitioning, quality-based selection, BAM_FDUP marking or removal, optical distance detection, optional DT tagging, Picard-shaped metrics and BAM/CRAM index output. MarkDuplicates defaults to Picard ADD_PG_TAG_TO_READS=true and CREATE_INDEX=false: it writes the configurable @PG header and record-level PG tag without creating an unexpected BAM index; pass --create-output-bam-index=true to opt into the index. It starts each output record with stale BAM_FDUP/DT cleared (Picard CLEAR_DT=true); --add-pg-tag=false suppresses the new PG header/tag.
GATK optional booleans for --add-pg-tag and --create-output-bam-index accept bare/true/1 or false/0 and reject other literals before processing records.

When --tmp-dir is provided, duplicate-key summaries spill to sorted binary runs and are looked up from disk during the second pass; oversized individual keys are chunked across runs and merged by key, and spill files are cleaned after a complete manifest. The representative uses Picard SUM_OF_BASE_QUALITIES (MAPQ excluded), and non-paired duplicates are not classified as optical; the pinned Picard oracle compares duplicate flags, DT tags and standard metrics columns. Metrics include a deterministic estimated library size with optical pairs excluded, one row per read-group library (LB), and the overlaid duplicate/optical/non-optical set-size histogram; cloud staging and remaining release-specific Picard metrics remain explicit fallback.

GATK/Picard TAGGING_POLICY supports DontTag, OpticalOnly, and All. OpticalOnly writes DT:Z:SQ only for optical duplicate records and leaves ordinary library duplicates untagged; both policies share the same duplicate classification and metrics path.

Paired ReadEnds are finalized from both mapped mates' actual unclipped five-prime coordinates after read-name pairing, including records without MC and terminal S/H clipping; a bounded pinned oracle covers the no-MC/clipped pair-key boundary.

The OutputManifest records runtime resource telemetry (RSS, scratch and spill-run bytes, spill run counts) via the shared ResourceSnapshot JSON, and the file-boundary benchmark (benchmark_mark_duplicates.py, warmup/p50/p95 with a forced spill run) is wired into verify_all.sh and both CTest backends.

Native prototype performs deterministic site-level shard merge, exact duplicate removal, true-coordinate-adjacent REF-only NON_REF block coalescing independent of depth metadata, repeatable -L/--intervals filtering with GATK UNION (default) or INTERSECTION set rules, and GT/DP/AD/PL sample-field merge with BGZF/Tabix or plain VCF/Tribble .idx output.

Multi-sample FORMAT merge supports disjoint sample headers with deterministic missing-value fill, including coalesced reference blocks; the pinned GATK 4.6.2.0 two-sample oracle checks indexed inputs, ALT/sample union, block coordinates and site-set exactness, while full GATK joint-genotyping/GenomicsDB semantics remain explicit fallback.

CombineGVCFs interval selection follows the GATK 4.6.2.0 reference-confidence boundary: a REF/<NON_REF> block whose END falls beyond an interval end is dropped (Java warns that the interval cuts a gVCF block), while a block whose END is contained is emitted in full; aggregate and --stream-merge share this predicate and the pinned interval-refblock oracle.

--sites-only-vcf-output uses a duplicated writer header and bcf_subset_format after merge/allele/FORMAT computation, producing the same 8-column site-only shape as GATK while preserving full sample payload during the merge stage.

PL-less reference-confidence input is preserved as PL-less output: when all merged sample calls lack FORMAT/PL, native does not synthesize missing PL vectors (.,.,.). Pure reference blocks also retain END without promoting sample FORMAT/DP to INFO/DP, matching the pinned GATK 4.6.2.0 oracle; PL-bearing remap paths remain unchanged.

GATK Boolean options --call-genotypes and --convert-to-base-pair-resolution accept bare/true/1 and false/0 through the shared optional-boolean parser; explicit false does not enable native experimental genotype materialization.
The OutputManifest records runtime resource telemetry via the shared ResourceSnapshot JSON, and the file-boundary benchmark (benchmark_combine_gvcfs.py, warmup/p50/p95) is wired into verify_all.sh.

The C++ Host adapter owns resource probing, batch-size/reader-thread/tmp-dir adaptation, deterministic fastgatk-inputs.tsv input indexing and workspace/manifest validation; local VCF/sample-map inputs are preflight-checked and non-empty workspaces require explicit --overwrite-existing-genomicsdb-workspace. Workspace writes use an atomic sibling-directory lock, so concurrent retry tasks fail closed with RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED and owner/path are recorded in the manifest. The default backend remains the configured GATK GenomicsDB/TileDB implementation; --fastgatk-native-workspace (or FASTGATK_GENOMICSDB_BACKEND=native) publishes a portable sparse workspace index consumed by native GenotypeGVCFs, explicitly marked non-TileDB and non-bit-identical. Native imports checkpoint each materialized input with size/mtime fingerprints; --resume-native-workspace reuses completed copies after a retry and removes the checkpoint only after record-index/metadata publication. Native sample-name-map inputs are validated as exactly two columns with unique names, and each mapped single-sample VCF/GVCF is rewritten only in the private materialized workspace so downstream sample columns match GATK without mutating the source.

--genomicsdb-update-workspace-path is forwarded to the external GATK backend and preserves the existing workspace input index/metadata; GATK reuses the initial import interval set during incremental update. In explicit native sparse mode, the existing input index plus new shards are atomically rebuilt and remain non-TileDB; opaque/partial workspaces fail closed. The pinned 4.6.2.0 update-workspace oracle covers external TileDB append and native sparse incremental rebuild.

Native sparse imports now apply -L/--intervals (including interval-list/BED selectors) to complete record spans before materialization, with GATK UNION/INTERSECTION selection and interval kept/skipped telemetry. A reference-confidence block is retained in full when its span overlaps the selector; copied VCF/CSI indexes are not reused after filtering or sample-name rewriting. Incremental native updates restore the initial interval set from workspace metadata, matching GATK's update boundary. The pinned 4.6.2.0 native interval oracle compares bridge-exported records.

The adapter preserves the complete argument vector, including release-specific GenomicsDB options. Set FASTGATK_GATK_BINARY to the pinned GATK launcher; --fallback remains available if the adapter binary/backend is unavailable.

Pinned GATK 4.6.2.0 import oracle reopens the adapter-published local workspace with GenotypeGVCFs; the isolated legacy-ABI bridge oracle exports a real workspace and compares bounded GT/AD/PL fields. These are local publication/reopen boundaries, not native TileDB storage parity.

Native Host prototype follows GATK's VariantAnnotator walker on its deterministic surfaces: --comp[:NAME] membership flags, --dbsnp DB flag plus rsID merge into the ID field, --resource:NAME/-E NAME.FIELD transfers (ID/ALT/FILTER special cases, A/R-counted INFO values mapped onto the input's minimum-representation biallelics with zero-fill for unmatched alleles), and -A Coverage from the site pileup. Matching mirrors VariantOverlapAnnotator.getRsID (unfiltered source records split to minimum-representation biallelics, exact ref+alt equality).

Header output reproduces htsjdk VCFEncoder ordering (sorted FORMAT/INFO groups with GATK's default-annotation canonical lines overriding redefinitions such as GQ, contigs last) and the VAExpression header rules including the 'Value transferred from another external VCF resource' fallback. The bundled GATK 4.6.2.0 oracle is byte-exact on these boundaries.
GATK's full -A annotation plugin surface (ReducibleAnnotation AS_* family, JEXL JumboExpression evaluation, comp allele-concordance subtleties beyond the resource mapping) remains explicit fallback.

Native Host prototype follows GATK's Funcotator on the VCF output surface with gencode + simpleXSV data sources: directory discovery <ds>/<Name>/<hg19|hg38>/<name>.config with DataSourceUtils key validation (gencode mandatory), gencode funcotations over GTF + transcript FASTA with CANONICAL/ALL transcript selection and the 22-field Gencode_<version>_* layout (classification, cDNA/codon/protein changes, gcContent 200bp window, 21bp reference context, other-transcripts summary), simpleXSV GENE_NAME keying with <name>_<column> fields and blank miss fill, and the FUNCOTATION VCF grammar (Number=A, per-ALT [block#block], '|'-joined sanitized values per FuncotatorUtils).

Already-annotated inputs (header 'Funcotator Version') are refused exactly as Funcotator.onTraversalStart; the header carries the Funcotator Version line, the FUNCOTATION field description and ##source=Funcotator in htsjdk order.  The bundled GATK 4.6.2.0 oracle (verify_funcotator_vcf_gatk_oracle.py: XSV hit/miss, transcript multi-block, --annotation-default) is byte-exact.
locatableXSV/VCF/COSMIC data sources, MAF/SEG renderers, FilterFuncotations and FuncotateSegments remain explicit fallback.
